chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In the heterolytic ionization of HCl in aqueous solution, which statement accurately describes the curved-arrow electron flow?

options.label: A
options.text: A lone pair on the water oxygen attacks the hydrogen atom of HCl as the H-Cl bonding pair departs onto chlorine.

options.label: B
options.text: Chlorine donates a lone pair to oxygen while hydrogen remains neutral.

options.label: C
options.text: A homolytic cleavage transfers single electrons to both oxygen and chlorine.

options.label: D
options.text: Hydrogen attacks oxygen forming a three-membered cyclic intermediate.

questions.correct_answer: A lone pair on the water oxygen attacks the hydrogen atom of HCl as the H-Cl bonding pair departs onto chlorine.
questions.explanation: Heterolytic ionization involves the oxygen lone pair abstracting a proton, with the H-Cl bonding electrons moving onto chlorine to form Cl⁻.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: During the reaction between BF₃ and NH₃, what is the nature of the key mechanistic step?

options.label: A
options.text: Electrophilic addition of boron into the N-H σ bond.

options.label: B
options.text: A 1,2-hydride shift from nitrogen to boron.

options.label: C
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of the nitrogen lone pair into the empty, unhybridized 2p orbital of boron to form a coordinate covalent bond.

options.label: D
options.text: Homolytic radical coupling of B• and N• radicals.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic attack of the nitrogen lone pair into the empty, unhybridized 2p orbital of boron to form a coordinate covalent bond.
questions.explanation: BF₃ has an empty 2p orbital on boron (sp² hybridized) which accepts the unshared sp³ electron pair from NH₃.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: When sodium amide (NaNH₂) deprotonates water, what is the rate-determining event?

options.label: A
options.text: Exergonic, barrier-free proton transfer from the O-H bond to the strongly basic nitrogen lone pair of NH₂⁻.

options.label: B
options.text: Solvent-assisted ionization of water to H⁺ and OH⁻ prior to attack.

options.label: C
options.text: Slow homolytic cleavage of the O-H bond to form OH• radicals.

options.label: D
options.text: Formation of a high-energy pentacoordinate nitrogen intermediate.

questions.correct_answer: Exergonic, barrier-free proton transfer from the O-H bond to the strongly basic nitrogen lone pair of NH₂⁻.
questions.explanation: The huge difference in pKa (15.7 for water vs 38 for ammonia) drives a rapid, diffusion-controlled proton transfer.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: When dimethyl ether is treated with cold concentrated H₂SO₄, what reactive intermediate is formed?

options.label: A
options.text: Protonated dimethyloxonium cation [(CH₃)₂OH⁺] stabilized by the bisulfate counterion.

options.label: B
options.text: A planar carbon-centered enolate anion.

options.label: C
options.text: Methyl carbocation (CH₃⁺) via C-O bond heterolysis.

options.label: D
options.text: Methoxy radical (CH₃O•) via homolytic cleavage.

questions.correct_answer: Protonated dimethyloxonium cation [(CH₃)₂OH⁺] stabilized by the bisulfate counterion.
questions.explanation: Strong acid protonates the weakly basic ether oxygen lone pair to generate a resonance-neutral oxonium ion.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: During the dissolution of solid NaCl in water, what mechanistic interaction drives lattice dissociation?

options.label: A
options.text: Electron transfer from chloride to sodium forming neutral atoms.

options.label: B
options.text: Proton transfer from water to chloride forming gaseous HCl.

options.label: C
options.text: Multiple water dipoles coordinate electrostatically around Na⁺ (via oxygen lone pairs) and Cl⁻ (via polar O-H hydrogens).

options.label: D
options.text: Covalent bond formation between sodium and oxygen.

questions.correct_answer: Multiple water dipoles coordinate electrostatically around Na⁺ (via oxygen lone pairs) and Cl⁻ (via polar O-H hydrogens).
questions.explanation: Ion-dipole solvation energy thermodynamically overcomes the crystal lattice energy of NaCl.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In the reaction of NH₄⁺ with OH⁻, what characterizes the transition state?

options.label: A
options.text: A pentacoordinate nitrogen with two full covalent bonds to hydrogen.

options.label: B
options.text: A linear [N···H···O] transition state with partial bond breaking to nitrogen and partial bond formation to oxygen.

options.label: C
options.text: A radical pair transition state [H₃N• ··· •OH].

options.label: D
options.text: A triangular cyclic 3-membered transition state involving nitrogen, oxygen, and sodium.

questions.correct_answer: A linear [N···H···O] transition state with partial bond breaking to nitrogen and partial bond formation to oxygen.
questions.explanation: Standard Brønsted acid-base transition states are linear with simultaneous proton transfer between electronegative heteroatoms.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: When methyllithium reacts with water, how is the electron density redistributed?

options.label: A
options.text: The polarized C-Li bonding electron pair acts as a carbon nucleophile, abstracting a proton from water to yield methane.

options.label: B
options.text: Water oxygen attacks lithium expelling a methyl cation.

options.label: C
options.text: A 1,2-alkyl migration from lithium to oxygen occurs.

options.label: D
options.text: Lithium donates an electron to water forming lithium hydride and hydroxyl radical.

questions.correct_answer: The polarized C-Li bonding electron pair acts as a carbon nucleophile, abstracting a proton from water to yield methane.
questions.explanation: The strongly polarized C-Li bond has high carbanionic character, readily donating its electron pair to abstract a proton.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: When NH₃ gas meets HCl gas, what is the fundamental mechanistic step?

options.label: A
options.text: Radical chain initiation via UV light absorption.

options.label: B
options.text: Concerted double bond migration across the N-Cl axis.

options.label: C
options.text: Electrocyclic ring closure to form cyclic ammonium chloride.

options.label: D
options.text: Direct nucleophilic attack by the nitrogen lone pair on the acidic proton of HCl with simultaneous chloride departure.

questions.correct_answer: Direct nucleophilic attack by the nitrogen lone pair on the acidic proton of HCl with simultaneous chloride departure.
questions.explanation: The gas-phase reaction is an elementary bimolecular proton transfer yielding ion pairs that condense into a solid crystal lattice.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: When acetone is treated with strong aqueous acid, which resonance-stabilized intermediate is generated?

options.label: A
options.text: Acetyl radical [(CH₃)₂C•-OH].

options.label: B
options.text: Hydroxyisopropyl carbocation / protonated oxocarbenium ion [(CH₃)₂C=OH⁺ ↔ (CH₃)₂C⁺-OH].

options.label: C
options.text: Dimethylcarbocation [(CH₃)₂C⁺].

options.label: D
options.text: Acetone enolate anion [CH₂=C(O⁻)CH₃].

questions.correct_answer: Hydroxyisopropyl carbocation / protonated oxocarbenium ion [(CH₃)₂C=OH⁺ ↔ (CH₃)₂C⁺-OH].
questions.explanation: Protonation on carbonyl oxygen yields an oxocarbenium ion where the positive charge is shared between oxygen and carbon.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In the combination of H⁺ with H₂O, what is the shape of the potential energy coordinate?

options.label: A
options.text: A multi-step coordinate involving a radical intermediate.

options.label: B
options.text: A double-well potential with a high activation barrier representing slow proton insertion.

options.label: C
options.text: A purely downhill, barrierless coordinate with zero activation energy (Ea ≈ 0) yielding the pyramidal H₃O⁺ ion.

options.label: D
options.text: An endothermic reaction coordinate requiring thermal activation.

questions.correct_answer: A purely downhill, barrierless coordinate with zero activation energy (Ea ≈ 0) yielding the pyramidal H₃O⁺ ion.
questions.explanation: Proton capture by a neutral water lone pair is barrierless in the gas phase and liquid phase, releasing substantial hydration enthalpy.

options.text: Hydrogen attacks oxygen forming a three-membered cyclic intermediate.

options.label: B
options.text: A homolytic cleavage transfers single electrons to both oxygen and chlorine.

options.label: C
options.text: Chlorine donates a lone pair to oxygen while hydrogen remains neutral.

options.label: D
options.text: A lone pair on the water oxygen attacks the hydrogen atom of HCl as the H-Cl bonding pair departs onto chlorine.

questions.correct_answer: A lone pair on the water oxygen attacks the hydrogen atom of HCl as the H-Cl bonding pair departs onto chlorine.
questions.explanation: Heterolytic ionization involves the oxygen lone pair abstracting a proton, with the H-Cl bonding electrons moving onto chlorine to form Cl⁻.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: During the reaction between BF₃ and NH₃, what is the nature of the key mechanistic step?

options.label: A
options.text: Electrophilic addition of boron into the N-H σ bond.

options.label: B
options.text: Homolytic radical coupling of B• and N• radicals.

options.label: C
options.text: A 1,2-hydride shift from nitrogen to boron.

options.label: D
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of the nitrogen lone pair into the empty, unhybridized 2p orbital of boron to form a coordinate covalent bond.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic attack of the nitrogen lone pair into the empty, unhybridized 2p orbital of boron to form a coordinate covalent bond.
questions.explanation: BF₃ has an empty 2p orbital on boron (sp² hybridized) which accepts the unshared sp³ electron pair from NH₃.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: When sodium amide (NaNH₂) deprotonates water, what is the rate-determining event?

options.label: A
options.text: Slow homolytic cleavage of the O-H bond to form OH• radicals.

options.label: B
options.text: Exergonic, barrier-free proton transfer from the O-H bond to the strongly basic nitrogen lone pair of NH₂⁻.

options.label: C
options.text: Solvent-assisted ionization of water to H⁺ and OH⁻ prior to attack.

options.label: D
options.text: Formation of a high-energy pentacoordinate nitrogen intermediate.

questions.correct_answer: Exergonic, barrier-free proton transfer from the O-H bond to the strongly basic nitrogen lone pair of NH₂⁻.
questions.explanation: The huge difference in pKa (15.7 for water vs 38 for ammonia) drives a rapid, diffusion-controlled proton transfer.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: When dimethyl ether is treated with cold concentrated H₂SO₄, what reactive intermediate is formed?

options.label: A
options.text: A planar carbon-centered enolate anion.

options.label: B
options.text: Methoxy radical (CH₃O•) via homolytic cleavage.

options.label: C
options.text: Methyl carbocation (CH₃⁺) via C-O bond heterolysis.

options.label: D
options.text: Protonated dimethyloxonium cation [(CH₃)₂OH⁺] stabilized by the bisulfate counterion.

questions.correct_answer: Protonated dimethyloxonium cation [(CH₃)₂OH⁺] stabilized by the bisulfate counterion.
questions.explanation: Strong acid protonates the weakly basic ether oxygen lone pair to generate a resonance-neutral oxonium ion.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: During the dissolution of solid NaCl in water, what mechanistic interaction drives lattice dissociation?

options.label: A
options.text: Covalent bond formation between sodium and oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: Proton transfer from water to chloride forming gaseous HCl.

options.label: C
options.text: Electron transfer from chloride to sodium forming neutral atoms.

options.label: D
options.text: Multiple water dipoles coordinate electrostatically around Na⁺ (via oxygen lone pairs) and Cl⁻ (via polar O-H hydrogens).

questions.correct_answer: Multiple water dipoles coordinate electrostatically around Na⁺ (via oxygen lone pairs) and Cl⁻ (via polar O-H hydrogens).
questions.explanation: Ion-dipole solvation energy thermodynamically overcomes the crystal lattice energy of NaCl.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In the reaction of NH₄⁺ with OH⁻, what characterizes the transition state?

options.label: A
options.text: A radical pair transition state [H₃N• ··· •OH].

options.label: B
options.text: A pentacoordinate nitrogen with two full covalent bonds to hydrogen.

options.label: C
options.text: A triangular cyclic 3-membered transition state involving nitrogen, oxygen, and sodium.

options.label: D
options.text: A linear [N···H···O] transition state with partial bond breaking to nitrogen and partial bond formation to oxygen.

questions.correct_answer: A linear [N···H···O] transition state with partial bond breaking to nitrogen and partial bond formation to oxygen.
questions.explanation: Standard Brønsted acid-base transition states are linear with simultaneous proton transfer between electronegative heteroatoms.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: When acetone is treated with strong aqueous acid, which resonance-stabilized intermediate is generated?

options.label: A
options.text: Hydroxyisopropyl carbocation / protonated oxocarbenium ion [(CH₃)₂C=OH⁺ ↔ (CH₃)₂C⁺-OH].

options.label: B
options.text: Dimethylcarbocation [(CH₃)₂C⁺].

options.label: C
options.text: Acetyl radical [(CH₃)₂C•-OH].

options.label: D
options.text: Acetone enolate anion [CH₂=C(O⁻)CH₃].

questions.correct_answer: Hydroxyisopropyl carbocation / protonated oxocarbenium ion [(CH₃)₂C=OH⁺ ↔ (CH₃)₂C⁺-OH].
questions.explanation: Protonation on carbonyl oxygen yields an oxocarbenium ion where the positive charge is shared between oxygen and carbon.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In the combination of H⁺ with H₂O, what is the shape of the potential energy coordinate?

options.label: A
options.text: A multi-step coordinate involving a radical intermediate.

options.label: B
options.text: A purely downhill, barrierless coordinate with zero activation energy (Ea ≈ 0) yielding the pyramidal H₃O⁺ ion.

options.label: C
options.text: An endothermic reaction coordinate requiring thermal activation.

options.label: D
options.text: A double-well potential with a high activation barrier representing slow proton insertion.

questions.correct_answer: A purely downhill, barrierless coordinate with zero activation energy (Ea ≈ 0) yielding the pyramidal H₃O⁺ ion.
questions.explanation: Proton capture by a neutral water lone pair is barrierless in the gas phase and liquid phase, releasing substantial hydration enthalpy.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: When methyllithium reacts with water, how is the electron density redistributed?

options.label: A
options.text: A 1,2-alkyl migration from lithium to oxygen occurs.

options.label: B
options.text: Water oxygen attacks lithium expelling a methyl cation.

options.label: C
options.text: Lithium donates an electron to water forming lithium hydride and hydroxyl radical.

options.label: D
options.text: The polarized C-Li bonding electron pair acts as a carbon nucleophile, abstracting a proton from water to yield methane.

questions.correct_answer: The polarized C-Li bonding electron pair acts as a carbon nucleophile, abstracting a proton from water to yield methane.
questions.explanation: The strongly polarized C-Li bond has high carbanionic character, readily donating its electron pair to abstract a proton.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: When NH₃ gas meets HCl gas, what is the fundamental mechanistic step?

options.label: A
options.text: Electrocyclic ring closure to form cyclic ammonium chloride.

options.label: B
options.text: Radical chain initiation via UV light absorption.

options.label: C
options.text: Concerted double bond migration across the N-Cl axis.

options.label: D
options.text: Direct nucleophilic attack by the nitrogen lone pair on the acidic proton of HCl with simultaneous chloride departure.

questions.correct_answer: Direct nucleophilic attack by the nitrogen lone pair on the acidic proton of HCl with simultaneous chloride departure.
questions.explanation: The gas-phase reaction is an elementary bimolecular proton transfer yielding ion pairs that condense into a solid crystal lattice.
